Clear foreground silhouette, continuous playable plane, midground organ silhouettes and distant blue organ depth. Natural coherent organic paths with recognizable landmarks recurring across adjacent views. No labels or text; annotations will be applied separately. This is an art direction concept, not a collision map. Very wide panoramic landscape. An entirely NEW lateral-oblique cutaway of ONE colossal dead fictional baleen whale 120 metres long, head LEFT, soft horizontal tail flukes RIGHT, both within margins. 0.30m explorer is only an almost invisible amber speck, one or two specks total. Unbroken outer silhouette and continuous dorsal vertebrae connect the whole body. Important clear macro anatomy: huge long mouth occupies left 26%, only upper jaw has fine baleen, broad tongue below; compact small paired blowholes on head surface, not tall pipes, mouth/nasal passages separated by intact palate except a lateral wound. Small auditory bulla behind lower skull, no giant cochlea; exploration surrounds it. Thorax 27–46%: tall ribs only here, blue collapsed lung dorsally, inert muted red heart lower and anterior; curved thick diaphragm at 46%. Abdomen 46–66%: ochre fore-stomach immediately behind diaphragm, olive intestinal loops farther rear; stomach entrance via narrow longitudinally split esophageal margin from mouth, not a giant open hallway replacing the lungs. Dorsal paravertebral exterior corridor runs along 28–82%, outside solid vertebrae, NOT spinal canal. No ribs rear of thorax. Tail stock 83–100% dense parallel muscle/tendons, no bones inside horizontal fluke. Paint thin discoverable shelf routes and occasional repaired torn membranes; routes leave and rejoin around organs instead of threading every chamber on one line. Make the diaphragm wound visibly a separate stomach-to-lung branch, and upper return along trachea toward head visibly distinct from digestive route. At posterior spine fork, left-going route follows long dorsal spine toward head, right-going route follows tapering tail; never put head ear beside tail. Whole world shares same water haze and repeated landmark spine/rib system. Large organs dwarf tiny playable shelves; huge corpse on dark deep seabed. Dead organs do not breathe or beat; no blood, waterfalls, air waterline, arrows, panel boundaries. Main goal: a single coherent explorable world whose zones flow physically into one another, not a page of separate area paintings.
